records.evidence_span: Here, we present the first global, wall-to-wall canopy height map at 10 m ground sampling distance for the year 2020.
limitations: The AOI is the Batch 01 OSM-derived pilot bbox, not an official ward boundary or full-ward coverage.

Canopy height is a 2020 global model inferred from Sentinel-2 imagery with sparse GEDI supervision; it is not an individual-tree inventory, urban airborne LiDAR, field survey, or current-condition measurement.
The standard-deviation layer is predictive model uncertainty, not a survey-accuracy tolerance or confidence guarantee for individual pixels.
The AOI subset contains 10,883 nodata pixels (8.350918%); statistics exclude nodata and do not establish species, stem counts, crown geometry, or tree health.
The pixel-aligned derivative extends at most one native source pixel beyond each requested AOI edge.
records.resolution: 1/12000 degree pixels (0.0000833333333333 degree); 10 m ground sampling distance

JRC Global Surface Water is a Landsat-derived surface-water history product at nominal 30 m, not a drainage-network inventory, flood-depth or flood-extent model, rainfall-runoff model, calibrated hydraulic model, or elevation surface.
Occurrence describes observation frequency from March 1984 through December 2024; 2024 seasonality describes one calendar year and should not be treated as a guarantee of future permanence.
The normalized occurrence-change layer compares homologous months in 1984-1999 and 2000-2024; it does not attribute causes, prove a flood event, or validate water at parcel scale.
Version 1.5 uses Landsat Collection 2; the official update note says alignment changes are typically subpixel but can reach or exceed one 30 m pixel in some WRS-2 path/rows.
The pixel-aligned derivative extends at most one native source pixel beyond each requested AOI edge.
